title: WORK-LAB logical model provider registry — the only model identifiers projects may reference
purpose: Projects (ArcheAxis-Knowledge-OS, WORK-LAB, DESIGN-LAB) call these logical provider ids. A provider id hides the runtime, the file name, the quantization and every absolute path. Physical binding lives in model-registry.json + runtime-registry.json.

providers.display_name: Local FAST (quick classification / extraction / rewrite / routing)

required_request_options.why: Measured on LM Studio 0.4.25: qwen3.5-4b IGNORES both chat_template_kwargs {enable_thinking:false} and the /no_think prompt token (reasoning_content consumed the whole max_tokens budget, content empty; reproduced 3x). reasoning_effort="none" works (600 content chars, reasoning_tokens 0).

measured.runtime: lmstudio 0.4.25 (desktop), llama.cpp backend managed by LM Studio

providers.binding_note: Single physical copy in the shared library; LM Studio indexes the shared library root in place (downloadsFolder = the model library), so no import, copy or link exists. Ollama was NOT used for this weight (its CDN measured 136 KB/s here and the pull never completed).
providers.operationalStatus: OPERATIONAL 2026-09-29: server autostarts, self-heals every 10 minutes, and loads this model on demand without the user opening LM Studio.

negative_capabilities.why: Without reasoning_effort:'none' the model's reasoning_content consumes the entire max_tokens budget and the visible content comes back EMPTY (reproduced 3x). chat_template_kwargs{enable_thinking:false} and the /no_think token are both IGNORED here.

providers.standby_reason: Ollama 0.34.4 no longer resolves OLLAMA_MODELS to the shared library (see runtime-registry ollama.model_store_defect), so this weight is not served by any runtime right now. It is retained in place pending a user decision; it is NOT deleted and NOT counted as the WL-MODEL-02 'two general LLMs' target.
providers.binding_status_note: Separated from operationalStatus on 2026-10-01 (AG-05) because the two describe different things and reading operationalStatus alone wrongly implied the model was callable. The runtime endpoint is up; THIS BINDING IS NOT SERVED. Evidence: the weight is an Ollama blob under Model library\ollama\blobs (LM Studio indexes <publisher>/<repo>/<file>.gguf, not that layout), it is absent from runtime-registry lmstudio.model_index.verified_indexed_models, and model-registry states runtime="none (was ollama)".
providers.operationalStatus: RUNTIME endpoint scope only (2026-09-29): the LM Studio HTTP server is up, autostarts, and self-heals every 10 minutes, so the ENDPOINT accepts requests. This is not a claim that this provider's binding resolves — see binding_status above; it does not.

providers.display_name: Local DEEP (complex understanding / multi-document synthesis / deep reasoning)

required_request_options.why: Measured on LM Studio 0.4.25: unlike qwen3.5-4b, DEEP produced real content on ALL THREE channels (reasoning_effort=none: 84 content chars / 0 reasoning tokens; chat_template_kwargs enable_thinking=false: 56 chars / 57 reasoning tokens; no control: 64 chars / 141 reasoning tokens). reasoning_effort=none is recommended because it produced the least reasoning overhead.

measured.perf_note: LM Studio's default offload reaches 78% of llama.cpp's explicit -ngl 32 (2.52 tok/s) but is clearly better than -ngl 0 (1.32 tok/s). Explicit offload control remains superior for this memory-bandwidth-bound 13.27 GB model on an 8 GiB card.

providers.api_shape: openai-compatible /v1/completions driven by the model's own rerank chat template

measured.verdict: Correct on every case, including the hard distractor; but it returns only yes/no.

providers.runtime_note: ACTIVE BINDING = lmstudio (see binds_to_runtime). CORRECTED 2026-10-01 (AG-05e): this note previously said reranking 'is served by llama.cpp with --rerank --pooling rank', which described a DIFFERENT runtime than the one actually bound, and it also still narrated the removed Ollama server. Both were historical. The accurate position: LM Studio is the declared serving runtime and it has NO rerank endpoint and never returns logprobs (see runtime_limitation), so reranking here is a BINARY verdict produced through /v1/completions. llama.cpp is retained only as an optional, non-auto-starting escape hatch that CAN serve /v1/rerank with continuous scores; it is not bound and is not running.
providers.runtime_limitation: Measured on LM Studio 0.4.25: (a) there is NO rerank endpoint - /v1/rerank, /api/v0/rerank and GET /v1/rerank all return {"error":"Unexpected endpoint or method"}; (b) the API NEVER returns logprobs - /v1/completions with logprobs=20 returns "logprobs": null even for an already-loaded ordinary LLM (qwen3.5-4b), and /api/v0/completions behaves the same. Without logprobs only a hard yes/no verdict is obtainable, so ties between two accepted candidates cannot be ordered.

superseded_measurement.status: NOT REPRODUCIBLE ON LM STUDIO - retained only as the llama.cpp reference record, must not be cited as an LM Studio capability.

providers.fidelity_tradeoff: This is a real, recorded regression in fidelity versus the llama.cpp path: llama.cpp gives a continuous score (spread 0.9996, deterministically orderable), LM Studio gives a binary verdict. The capability is online and correct, but not equivalent.
providers.runtime_status: ONLINE and verified as a binary verdict (correct on every tested case), but NO score is exposed: LM Studio 0.4.25 has no rerank endpoint and never returns logprobs.
providers.operationalStatus: OPERATIONAL 2026-09-29: server autostarts, self-heals every 10 minutes, and loads this model on demand without the user opening LM Studio.
providers.runtime_note_history: Ollama 0.34.3 exposes NO rerank endpoint (probed: /api/rerank, /v1/rerank, /api/reranking all 404), so reranking is served by llama.cpp with --rerank --pooling rank.  [historical text, retained verbatim; both runtimes it names are either removed or unbound]

negative_capabilities.why: LM Studio 0.4.25 always returns a binary verdict here, so two ACCEPTABLE candidates cannot be ordered relative to each other. Ranking is filter-quality, not sort-quality.
negative_capabilities.evidence: runtime_limitation (a)+(b); fidelity_tradeoff records the regression vs the llama.cpp path
negative_capabilities.escape_hatch: llama.cpp is retained as an optional, non-auto-starting runtime that CAN serve /v1/rerank with continuous scores; it is not bound here.

negative_capabilities.why: The serving API never returns logprobs (logprobs=20 yields null even for an already-loaded ordinary LLM), so no numeric score is exposed to a caller.
/v1/rerank, /api/v0/rerank and GET /v1/rerank all return 'Unexpected endpoint or method'. The verdict is produced through /v1/completions instead.

providers.binding_note: Foreign key closed 2026-10-01 (AG-05). This previously read "qwen2.5vl-7b", which is the LEGACY Ollama BLOB name (model-registry previous_entry.id, and finalStructureTarget.ingestion[0] as an OCR candidate label). That blob has no vision projector and is NOT the served artifact. The live binding is the model-registry entry id "qwen2.5-vl-7b-instruct" (ggml-org/Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct-GGUF, Q4_K_M weights + paired mmproj), which is what LM Studio reports as type=vlm and what model_name_on_wire resolves to.
providers.provenance_note: Alternative to migrating the Ollama blob: that blob contains no vision projector (hasVision=false, no clip.* keys, single image.model layer, no mmproj anywhere in the library), so OCR could not be migrated. Downloaded from the llama.cpp project's own repository via hf-mirror.com (domestic route; huggingface.co direct was avoided on user instruction so the personal VPN is not consumed). 8 parallel ranged connections measured up to 13.4 MiB/s.

measured.verification: live vision call on the zh/en fixture, 2 independent runs
measured.comparison: The earlier Ollama qwen2.5vl:7b result was 6/6 in 61.7 s. This is 8/8 in 5.3 s and, unlike that blob, it genuinely has a vision projector.

operationalDeployment.summary: LM Studio runs as an unattended background service: autostart on launch, logon warm-up, 10-minute health check with self-heal, and just-in-time loading for the large models.
operationalDeployment.userActionRequired: none - call http://127.0.0.1:1234/v1 with the model name

negativeCapabilityVocabulary: Closed vocabulary for negative_capabilities[].state: UNAVAILABLE (measured to not work here), UNVERIFIED (not exercised, so must not be assumed), REFUSED (blocked by policy). Every entry carries why + evidence, and escape_hatch is null when no configured path exists. Added by AG-05f (2026-10-01) because the Atlas G05 acceptance wording explicitly requires 'negative 能力' and the registry previously expressed its limitations only in prose that a machine consumer could not read.
